So I'll throw in some tips just so this isn't just a humblebrag post.

I posted that I was going to attempt it many months back on this site before I deleted my account. I got a bit bored of XCom2 [which was my own fault for trying to beat it on hard with 0 fatalities] and only just re-installed it thinking I'd start a new campaign. Was gladdened to find I had actually played a very tight game about 1/3 of the way through the campaign that I had completely forgotten about. It must have been a drunk marathon weekend or something. No clever customizations or outrageous color schemes [like the bald Heavy Trooper with the Cigar named Kojak, or the Ranger named Obama with the voice selection that sounds kinda like Obama..]

This crew was totally stock with game generated nicknames, and they were kicking ass. I guess I must have spent more time on strat than flair.

Anyway just completed it tonight. The only real difficulty I had in the last 2/3 of the campaign was the first time the Avatar appeared. I am a bit stubborn so I won't allow myself to fail a mission even if it has a super-plot on top of it. [Remember you have to spike a Codex brain to hack into their Psi-Net and the Avatar portals in]

He is a real pain in the ass to kill if you don't have any anti-psionics, which I didn't. [I never made a Mind-Shield, can you even make one in this game?]

So to kill an Avatar you really need to spread your guys out so you can just keep pinging him. My Heavy Trooper "Boom Boom" had extra explosives, range, etc and 2x Acid Bombs and 2x Incendiary Bombs. I had to reload about 5 times the first time I met one. But by the end of the game, I didn't have to reload on the last 2 missions once. A big part of that was having the "Soothing Aura" or whatever on my fully loaded Witch.

For the end game battle when you have the arena where the portals from the different world are spewing out endless enemies and the 3 Avatars, the simple way to beat it - don't play in their arena.

I positioned two snipers above the "Human Science Environment" outside the entrance to the "Arena". I put my 2 techs on either side of the door but down on the lower walkway, kept a heavy running interference in opening of the doorway and send my Commander-Avatar and my Witch ["Grim"] into the arena to draw them out. It is easy to mind-control Mutons and other dumb beasts, so they kept a nice scouting view and gave me plenty of time to retreat back through the hallway out of the Arena luring everything to its death. In the final battle I only ever had one unit Mind-Controlled, and only for half a turn as "Grim" was nearby to break him out of it. This heavy hit one of the Avatars with "Rupture" which made him easy to finish off. You have to knock down their armor [I had 3 war suits for my heavy and two specialists, 2 wraith suits for my "Zone Control" Sniper ["Deadeye"] and "Grim" so she could move around wherever her Psionic powers were needed, and so that "Deadeye" could always get up top. The backup sniper "Scratch" was setup like a wild-west shooter which didn't actually come in at all useful in the endgame, but made him very versatile as a forward sniper - having no squadsight-overwatch but plenty of different ways to shoot his sidearm. Of the two technicians I took into the endgame, one was my uber-medic ["Broker"] and the other was my combat-hacker ["Jammer"]. "Jammer" actually finished off the 3rd Avatar with a Mark III Gremlin's combat move.

As you are fighting the Avatars in the entrance to their Arena, about half the time they will actually teleport outside into the lab where they can easily be picked off.

Other random tips:

I hated the secure the VIP missions [especially the non-compliant ones you had to knock out and carry]. I found these missions to become quite simple with a Ranger who could re-cloak for scouting and a grapple. You can use the grapple with the VIP on your shoulder to get to evac, easy as pie.

Any time you have to place X4, you can simply use one unit with a Wraith suit, some battle scanners, and movement bonuses. Well - you can, until you can't any more. The last X4 placement mission [I think it was the blacksite-vial mission, I did them "out of order" because of how I had secured the strategy map] Anyway I did a few just by wraith-running through the wall and then back out to evac. But the last one had one of those Psi-Spheres that can one-shot anything waiting inside by the demolition point. Did not go well, had to bring in the troops for that one. Lots of bodies.

  • Can't emphasize enough to get a viable Psi-Trooper going early in the game. I had one who I used carefully, and I only ever developed a 2nd one very late in the game who I only used on one mission.

The stats at the end are very helpful in remembering how you played through. I basically went for armor quicker than "World". At the end of the game I had 18 units, about 12 of them were max level. I got the Advanced Warfare Center a little late, really should have gotten it earlier so I would have developed more extra perks. But by end-game [in fact the last 3 story-missions] I had a number of technicians and heavies who had "Ever Vigilant" which is a game changer - you can sprint into forward positions and still get Overwatch. That combined with the Specialist "Aid" buff that grants overwatch and you can control the board.

Although I utilized 3 W.A.R. suits, not once in the game did I use their "fortress" mode. I don't understand the point, if you can't find good cover you don't have good enough map-awareness or enough mobility. I also never used the "Reaper" ability on my primary ranger ["Judgement Day"] but it has a cool icon. [It's a guaranteed hit with your sword, and if you get a kill, you get another action but with less melee damage]. Similarly, I never used the Sniper action that is similar, if you get a kill after activating it you can shoot again every time you get a kill.

The armory is very useful. There are a ton of specialized tools that can make some very deadly builds. I had 5 different types of specialized ammo, 4 different types of armor augmentation, and 5 different heavy weapon types at the end. And it is well worth your time to make sure you are sharing your best-upgraded guns with the right people. Pairing the weapon upgrades with the right ammo, for example the "Talon" Rounds with advanced laser, because Talon rounds buff crits while the laser helps you get them. A ranger with advanced laser and talon rounds can one shot half the enemies in the game. By the end I wasn't messing with Bluescreen rounds, but they are very useful especially when you are still using ballistic weapons. By the end I was using armor piercing, dragon rounds, and tracers.

  • Even after the debuff the "Mimic" beacon is a life-saver. If I do another playthrough [Long-War, with mods installed etc] I am considering making a lean squad of psi-users and rangers and just using mimic-beacons to draw everything into traps and complete as many missions as I can without engaging. I was very disappointed with the prox-mines, but I think I read somewhere you can get "Prox-Bombs" but I still don't think those would be very useful. Why not just throw a grenade at it and be done. On that note, the EMP-Bomb is the bomb so you don't have to use Bluescreen rounds or bring a combat-specialist along to deal with robots. I didn't hack a single Robot, didn't even have the perk to do so. I just shot at them.

Hope this was useful for someone.

-Analek
